caption:
Please don’t come @ me with peppers being higher in vitamin C, we’re here for function AND flavor. 

My mother-in laws Preserved Lemons:

Ingredients (for 1 jar)
 • 1 lemon (or 2–4 if using a bigger jar)
 • coarse sea salt 
 • olive oil, enough to fully cover

 1. Take a clean glass jar (you can sterilize it once with boiling water and let it dry.)
 2. Wash the lemons and slice them into thin rounds. Clean hands.
 3. Start layering: lemon slices, a good pinch of salt, lemon, salt - keep going until everything is packed in.
 4. Press everything down firmly so the lemons start releasing their juice.
 5. Pour olive oil over the top until everything is completely covered. (the lemons should always stay under the oil.)
 6. Close the jar and keep it in a cool place.

They’ll be ready after about 3 days. Over time (1–2 weeks), they get more mellow and develop a deeper, slightly fermented flavor.

Use the peel and the flesh in salads, grains, roasted veg and the oil on top is honestly one of the best parts.

*feel free to play around with the flavor base. Try peppercorns, bay leaves, garlic or mustard seeds, and a little chili for heat. Just keep it balanced so the lemons stay the main character.
author: Raquels Pantry

title: Mother-in-Law's Easy Preserved Lemons
one_liner: A simple preserved lemon recipe that boosts flavor and enhances plant-based iron absorption via vitamin C.
key_points: Layer lemon rounds with coarse salt, press down, cover fully with olive oil, and cure for 3+ days
The longer they sit (1–2 weeks), the more mellow and fermented the flavor becomes
Use the peel, flesh, and infused oil in salads, grains, and roasted veg
Customize with peppercorns, bay leaves, garlic, chili, or mustard seeds while keeping lemons the star

ingredients: coarse sea salt, several generous pinches
olive oil, enough to fully cover lemons
instructions: Sterilize a clean glass jar with boiling water and let it dry.
Wash lemons and slice into thin rounds.
Layer lemon slices and a good pinch of salt alternately until the jar is packed.
Press everything down firmly so lemons begin releasing their juice.
Pour olive oil over the top until all lemons are completely submerged.
Seal the jar and store in a cool place for at least 3 days before using.
